The third preview of CoSky 8.0. There is still **no compatibility promise**: the API, the wire format and the Redis keys may change before the beta, and nothing here is ready for real traffic. The stable release is still 6.x, on the [`v6`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/tree/v6) branch.

**If you try 8.0, use this one rather than `8.0.0-alpha.1` or `8.0.0-alpha.2`.** Both of those can leave an application on values that no longer exist.

## Fixed

- **A deleted Config's values leave the application.** They used to stay until a restart, because a Spring Cloud refresh only adds and replaces property sources. It also happened when an application started from a snapshot the server no longer agreed with, such as after Redis lost its data, and when a Config lost a YAML document or all its content. An `optional:` Config now takes its values with it. A required one keeps its last values, having nothing to fall back on.
- **A refresh is no longer missed under a revision seen before.** A Redis that lost writes hands a revision out a second time, so the application now compares the whole Config.
- **Redis no longer fills up with large Configs.** The change log is limited in bytes as well as in entries, by `cosky.watch.window-bytes`, 64 MB per namespace by default. Writing a 1 MB Config 800 times took 825 MB, and now takes 92 MB. There is no new setting, and write speed showed no visible difference.
- **Signing out during a token renewal stays signed out,** and pasting something shaped like an ID token into the sign-in page is refused like any other bad token. These came in just after `8.0.0-alpha.2` was prepared.

## Upgrading from an earlier alpha

Nothing to do. A log written before this has no byte count yet, so its older entries are not counted until they are trimmed, and this corrects itself as the log turns over.

## Known limits

To be settled before the beta:

- **Propagation at 20,000 connections** is only borderline, when every write goes to every connection: a p99 of 171 to 525 ms in 6 runs of 7, against a target of 500 ms. The other run reached 5.8 seconds, and we do not know why.
- **A replica cut off from Redis on its own** goes on serving what it last knew, and stays ready. [Deployment](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment) shows how to notice.
- **Not yet tried:** OIDC providers other than Keycloak, `kubectl drain` with several nodes, a real network between the parts, or Redis Cluster at this scale.
